newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour hoodwinking public on tax - Waldegrave.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour hoodwinking public on tax - Waldegrave.

text.p: Treasury Chief Secretary William Waldegrave, seizing on reports of conflict between Labour leader Tony Blair and economics spokesman Gordon Brown, accused the opposition party on Friday of trying to "hoodwink" the British public on tax.

Reports in two tabloid newspapers -- the Sun and the Daily Express -- said Blair was set to block an announcement by Brown that he planned a 50 percent rate of tax on incomes above 100,000 stg a year.
They said Blair could see no reason to raise the rate from 40 percent as Labour had made no spending commitments which would justify a higher tax take.
"Gordon Brown clearly wants to be more frank and admit that Labour would put up taxes," Waldegrave said in a statement. "But it seems that Mr Brown is being blocked by the Labour leader."
"Labour should stop trying to hoodwink the British public on tax. They should now come clean and admit that there would be a tax hike under a Labour government."
